cf.title: Extend skipping FK checks on replicas to include ADD FK and TRUNCATE

input.subject: [PATCH] Extending FK check skipping on replicas to ADD FK and TRUNCATE

verdict_reasoning: The proposal fails at level 1b, so design objections are not ranked. prior-attempts-1: [P9] proposed the same truncate change and was closed as not needed, and this thread names no workflow that needs it. maintenance-fit-2: the proposal states no rule for which DDL checks session_replication_role = replica may skip. security-2: the back-patch request in message #2 would widen existing grants on the setting. A new version can answer all three, so the list should settle them before code review.

brief.title: Skip FK checks for add foreign key and truncate under session_replication_role = replica
brief.problem: With session_replication_role = replica, DML skips foreign key checks, but alter table ... add foreign key still validates existing rows and truncate of a referenced table is still blocked. The author says validation can take tens of days when the referenced table has hundreds of billions of rows. This hurts logical replication setups that load data first and add constraints later.
brief.proposed_design: When session_replication_role is replica, add foreign key skips the check of existing rows and truncate skips the error for referencing foreign keys. The patch wraps two code sections in tablecmds.c in a test of the role and adds regression tests.
user_visible_surface: Changed behavior of session_replication_role = replica: alter table ... add foreign key no longer validates existing rows.
Changed behavior of session_replication_role = replica: truncate on a table referenced by foreign keys no longer fails.
author_claims: Validation on huge referenced tables can take tens of days and is not needed when data comes from a known good source.
Truncate adds no new risk, since delete under replica role can already leave orphan rows.
The current behavior is a bug and should be back-patched to all supported branches.
Replica setup gets faster when the primary key index and foreign keys are created after the initial copy.
Existing documentation may already cover the change, so no docs update may be needed.
brief.thread_state: Rafia Sabih showed that add foreign key now accepts a row with no matching key, and the author replied this is intended. Nobody else has reviewed the design; the author asked Álvaro for review, and the other replies are about email reply style.
unclear: The patch does not say whether the new constraint is marked as validated in pg_constraint even though rows were never checked.
The proposal does not say how this differs from adding the constraint with not valid and validating later.
The patch has no documentation change for session_replication_role.
The proposal does not say whether truncate cascade or truncate of partitioned tables changes.
The patch does not say whether this applies to add foreign key on partitioned tables or to validate constraint.
The proposal does not say what privilege, beyond setting session_replication_role, is needed to bypass the checks.

prior_attempts.title: TRUNCATE behavior when session_replication_role = replica
prior_attempts.quote: This part of the patch didn't end up being necessary, since the updated implementation of logical decoding of TRUNCATE could do without it.
prior_attempts.reason: Peter Eisentraut argued that the current DELETE behaviour, which lets replicas hold data that violates foreign keys, is bad and should not be extended to TRUNCATE. He also saw no case for the change being needed. He closed the entry because the updated implementation of logical decoding of TRUNCATE no longer needed it.
prior_attempts.what_is_different: The truncate change is the same. This proposal also skips validation of existing rows in add foreign key and asks for a back-patch as a bug fix.

objections.title: Earlier objection to extending replica-role FK bypass to truncate is unanswered
objections.failure_scenario: An operator sets session_replication_role = replica in a migration script, runs truncate on a referenced table and then add foreign key. Both succeed, so orphan rows sit under a constraint the planner and users trust. Nobody finds out until a join drops rows or a later validate constraint or restore fails.
objections.argument: [P9] proposed the same truncate change. Per the AI summary of its thread, the objection was that the current DELETE behaviour is bad and should not be extended, and that no need was shown. Messages #1 and #8 use DELETE as the justification, which is the argument [P9]'s objector did not accept, and this proposal extends the bypass further to add foreign key. No reply in the thread addresses that earlier reasoning.
objections.author_must_show: Why should the replica-role bypass grow when the earlier objection was that the existing DELETE bypass is already harmful, and which workload needs truncate here?

critic.reasoning: [P9] proposed the same truncate change, and its verbatim key sentence says the change was not needed. Messages #1 and #8 justify truncate only by comparison with delete and name no workflow that needs it.

objections.title: session_replication_role grows from trigger firing into DDL bypass
objections.failure_scenario: Once add foreign key and truncate skip checks under replica role, the next requests are add check, not null, unique and exclusion validation, because the same argument fits each one. Each one adds a special case in a different command. No test fails when a new constraint path does not follow the rule, so the behaviour drifts.
objections.argument: Today the setting only controls which triggers fire, and foreign keys are skipped because they are triggers, as the docs quoted in message #1 say. This patch adds checks of the setting inside tablecmds.c, so the setting becomes a general unsafe-load switch with no defined edges. [P9] proposed the same truncate change and was not accepted. Its summarized reason was that the delete behaviour should not be extended. That summary is model-written, so it is a pointer only.
objections.author_must_show: What rule decides which DDL checks session_replication_role = replica may skip, and how does it stop later special cases for other constraint types?

critic.reasoning: The docs tie the foreign key effect to trigger firing, and the patch tests the setting inside tablecmds.c without stating a rule for which checks it may skip. [P9] is an AI summary about truncate only and must not be used as support here.

objections.title: Back-patching widens what existing grants on session_replication_role allow
objections.failure_scenario: An admin ran grant set on parameter session_replication_role to a non-superuser load role for faster DML. After a minor upgrade, that role, with only truncate privilege on a referenced table, can truncate it while other owners' tables still reference it. Today that needs truncate privilege on the referencing tables through cascade.
objections.argument: Message #2 asks to back-patch to all supported branches, so a grant made under the old meaning would change meaning silently. Truncate is a separate privilege from delete, so the comparison with delete in message #8 does not cover a role that holds truncate but not delete. The patch has no documentation change telling admins that the setting now also bypasses these checks.
objections.author_must_show: Which role holding set on session_replication_role but not superuser gains new power under this patch, and why is that safe to give out in a minor release?

critic.reasoning: A role with set on the parameter and truncate privilege only on the referenced table gains a new ability. The delete comparison in message #8 does not cover it, and the proposal does not discuss privileges.

other_surviving.title: Unchecked foreign keys recorded as validated, beside the existing not valid path
other_surviving.failure_scenario: A user runs alter table ... add foreign key under replica role on a table with orphan rows. The constraint looks like a normal, checked one. Later pg_dump emits the foreign key in post-data, and restoring into a normal session fails at that step, long after the original mistake.
other_surviving.argument: Postgres already has a spelling for adding a foreign key without checking existing rows: `not valid`, followed by `validate constraint`. It records the unchecked state in pg_constraint. The proposal does not say whether convalidated is set, and the example in message #1 shows a plain add foreign key succeeding. The planner trusts validated foreign keys for join estimates. Message #8 answers that delete under replica role already allows orphan rows, but that path never creates a constraint that claims to be checked.
other_surviving.author_must_show: Why is `add foreign key ... not valid` not enough for the replica setup case, and what does pg_constraint record under the patch?

critic.reasoning: `not valid` skips the same scan, and the proposal neither compares itself with it nor says what pg_constraint records. A new version can state the catalog state and the case `not valid` cannot serve, so this is fixable.

other_surviving.not_ranked_reason: level 2 is above the failing level 1b: not evaluated (base-up stop rule)

other_surviving.title: Logical replication apply would stop rejecting truncates that break subscriber FKs
other_surviving.failure_scenario: A subscriber has a local table with a foreign key to a replicated table. The publisher runs truncate on that replicated table. Today the apply worker, which runs with session_replication_role = replica, stops with an FK error; with the patch it truncates, and the subscriber's local rows silently point at nothing.
other_surviving.argument: The apply worker always runs as replica and replays truncate with restrict behaviour, so it could take the same path as a user's truncate. If the bypass sits on that shared path, the publisher gains the power to break the subscriber's own constraints, and the subscriber owner gets no error and no choice. Message #1 and message #9 discuss only manual sessions. [P9] says the decoding of truncate was built to work without this bypass.
other_surviving.author_must_show: Does the new truncate bypass apply inside the logical replication apply worker, and if so, why should a publisher be able to orphan subscriber-local referencing rows?

critic.reasoning: The apply worker runs with session_replication_role = replica and replays truncate through the shared truncate code with restrict behaviour. The logical replication docs say such an apply fails today, and the proposal does not mention this case.

other_surviving.not_ranked_reason: level 2 is above the failing level 1b: not evaluated (base-up stop rule)

other_surviving.title: Back-patching changes truncate and add foreign key in minor releases
other_surviving.failure_scenario: A site runs a maintenance script with session_replication_role = replica and relies on truncate failing on a referenced table. After a minor upgrade, truncate succeeds and the referencing rows are left without parents. The site finds out later from application errors.
other_surviving.argument: Message #2 asks to treat this as a bug and back-patch it to all supported branches. The behaviour has been the same since at least v13, so users may depend on it. A behaviour change that removes an error is a feature change, and minor releases do not normally carry those.
other_surviving.author_must_show: Which documented promise does the current behaviour break, so that a minor-release change in error behaviour is justified?

critic.reasoning: Message #2 asks for a back-patch to all supported branches, and no later message withdraws it. The change removes two errors that are stable since at least v13, which minor releases do not normally do.

other_surviving.not_ranked_reason: level 2 is above the failing level 1b: not evaluated (base-up stop rule)

refuted.title: Silent change to what replica role means for existing tools and scripts
refuted.failure_scenario: A replication tool or migration script already sets session_replication_role = replica and runs DDL in the same session. After a minor release, its add foreign key no longer rejects bad data, and truncate no longer refuses referenced tables. Nobody finds out until queries return orphan rows.
refuted.argument: session_replication_role controls which triggers fire, and the current docs describe its foreign key effect in those terms. The patch extends it to DDL validation and to truncate, but the documentation stays unchanged (message #1). Message #2 asks to back-patch this to all supported branches. That would change behaviour in a minor release, and no user asked for or controls the change.
refuted.author_must_show: Which existing users of replica role run add foreign key or truncate, and why is an opt-in option worse than changing the GUC's meaning in back branches?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of maintenance-fit-3 for the back-patch part and of maintenance-fit-2 for the change in what the setting means.

refuted.title: Truncate exemption repeats a proposal that was rejected before
refuted.failure_scenario: A user runs truncate on a referenced table under replica role, and every referencing row becomes an orphan in one statement. The proposal does not say what happens with truncate cascade or with partitioned tables, so the result in those cases is not defined.
refuted.argument: [P9] proposed the same truncate exemption. The objection recorded there, an AI summary, was that letting delete break foreign keys on replicas is undesirable and should not be extended. Message #1 uses the same argument [P9] faced, that delete already allows this. The proposal does not say what has changed since then, for example a logical replication case that needs it now.
refuted.author_must_show: Which current replication or apply workflow needs truncate of a referenced table under replica role, and how does it differ from the case set aside in [P9]?

refuted.title: Unchecked foreign key is stored as validated in pg_constraint
refuted.failure_scenario: A user sets session_replication_role = replica and adds a foreign key over a table that holds orphan rows. Months later pg_dump runs, and the restore fails at the add foreign key step. The planner may also use the bad constraint for join estimates in the meantime.
refuted.argument: Message #7 shows the command succeeds with a row that has no match, and message #8 says this is intended. The proposal does not say whether convalidated is set to true. If it is, the catalog records a guarantee that was never checked, and pg_dump, restore and the planner all trust that flag. Today `not valid` already skips the check and records the truth, and the proposal does not say why that is not enough.
refuted.author_must_show: Is the constraint marked convalidated after the skipped check, and if so, why is add foreign key ... not valid not the right tool?

refuted.title: Subscriber apply of truncate would stop failing and leave orphans
refuted.failure_scenario: A subscriber has a local table with a foreign key to a replicated table. The publisher truncates the replicated table. Today the apply worker stops with an error. With the patch it truncates, and the local referencing rows become orphans that nobody is told about.
refuted.argument: Logical replication apply workers run with session_replication_role = replica, so the patch changes truncate apply on every subscriber, not only manual bulk loads. The proposal describes only interactive use and does not mention apply workers. [P9] proposed the same truncate change. Its summary reports an objection to extending the delete behavior and says logical decoding of truncate was later built without it.
refuted.author_must_show: What should the apply worker do when a replicated truncate hits a local foreign key on the subscriber, and has that case been tested?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of security-1, which states the same apply worker case without asserting where the patch places the test.

refuted.title: Back-patching changes replica-role semantics in minor releases
refuted.failure_scenario: A publisher and subscriber run different minor releases of the same branch. One subscriber errors on a truncate that another subscriber accepts. An operator who relied on add foreign key rejecting bad rows under the replica role finds the error gone after a minor update.
refuted.argument: Message #2 asks to treat this as a bug and back-patch it to all supported branches. The current behavior has been stable since at least v13 (message #2), and the documentation does not promise the new behavior. Changing what persistent constraints guarantee in a minor release is a compatibility change, and so far one reviewer has questioned the design (message #7).
refuted.author_must_show: Which user relied on the current behavior being a bug, and why is a master-only change not enough?

refuted.title: Unchecked constraint may be recorded as validated, duplicating NOT VALID
refuted.failure_scenario: A user adds a foreign key under replica role on rows that do not match, and pg_constraint marks it validated. The planner uses validated foreign keys in join selectivity estimates, so plans quietly use wrong estimates. Any later feature that trusts convalidated, such as FK-based join removal, would return wrong results, and nobody would find out until a query result was wrong.
refuted.argument: Postgres already supports adding a foreign key without checking rows: `add foreign key ... not valid`, then `validate constraint` later. The proposal does not say why that path is not enough, or whether the new constraint is marked validated. If it is, convalidated stops meaning "checked", and every future user of that flag inherits the risk. In message #7 Rafia Sabih showed an unmatched row being accepted, and message #8 replies that this is intended. That reply does not address the catalog flag.
refuted.author_must_show: Is the constraint marked convalidated, and what does this give that `not valid` plus a later or skipped `validate constraint` does not?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of standards-compat-1. The added scenario about FK-based join removal concerns a feature that does not exist.

refuted.title: add foreign key ... not valid already skips the existing-row check
refuted.failure_scenario: An operator sets session_replication_role = replica, adds a foreign key on a table that holds orphan rows, and gets a constraint marked as validated. The planner and later DDL trust that flag, and pg_dump writes it out as a normal valid constraint. The orphan rows surface only when a restore or a later check fails.
refuted.argument: Postgres already has `alter table ... add foreign key ... not valid`, which skips the check of existing rows that message #1 calls slow, and `validate constraint` can run later. The only thing the patch adds beyond that is a constraint that claims to be validated without any check, and message #8 confirms orphan rows are accepted. The proposal does not compare itself with not valid at all, so a committer would likely see it as a second, less honest way to do the same job.
refuted.author_must_show: What does the replication setup need that `add foreign key ... not valid` cannot give, other than a validated flag that no check has confirmed?

refuted.title: truncate of a referenced table is already covered by delete
refuted.failure_scenario: A user under replica role truncates a referenced table by mistake and leaves every referencing row orphaned, with no error. Today the same intent needs an explicit delete, or `truncate ... cascade`, which also empties the referencing tables.
refuted.argument: Message #1 says delete under replica role already gives the same result, only slower, so the need is met today. The extra gain is speed on a step that, per message #9, mainly runs during initial setup. [P9] proposed the same truncate change and was closed. Its record says the change was not needed once logical decoding of truncate was done, and that extending the delete behaviour was judged bad.
refuted.author_must_show: Which real workflow needs truncate of a referenced table under replica role, where delete or truncate cascade is not workable, and how does it differ from the case closed in [P9]?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of prior-attempts-1. Its own claim that delete meets the need is weak, since delete on a very large table costs far more than truncate.

refuted.title: Existing not valid option already covers the add foreign key case
refuted.failure_scenario: A user setting up a large replica can already run alter table ... add foreign key ... not valid, which skips the scan of existing rows. The patch adds a second, silent way to get the same speed, and the constraint may then look validated without any row having been checked.
refuted.argument: The only demand in the thread is the author's extreme case of hundreds of billions of rows in message #1, with no field report, no -general thread and no second user. The proposal does not compare itself with not valid, which avoids the scan and records the truth in pg_constraint. Without a case that not valid cannot serve, a committer would likely see a new behaviour that only a small group needs.
refuted.author_must_show: Which replica setup workflows cannot use add foreign key ... not valid today, and which users other than the author have hit this?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of standards-compat-1, which asks the same question about `not valid`.

refuted.title: No user need shown for truncate on referenced tables under replica
refuted.failure_scenario: An operator runs truncate on a referenced table in a replica-role session and leaves orphan rows in every referencing table. Nothing reports it until a later join or a validate constraint fails.
refuted.argument: Message #1 justifies the truncate change only by symmetry with delete, and gives no workflow that needs it. [P9] proposed the same truncate change and was closed: the objector saw no need and did not want to extend the delete behaviour, and logical decoding of truncate did not require it. The material does not show what has changed since then.
refuted.author_must_show: What real replication or load workflow needs truncate of a referenced table under session_replication_role = replica, given that [P9] found none?

refuted.title: Existing replica-role users bear a behaviour change they did not ask for
refuted.failure_scenario: A replication tool or migration script runs its schema DDL in a session with session_replication_role = replica. After a minor release with the proposed back-patch, add foreign key accepts invalid existing rows without a warning. The users find out when queries return orphan rows.
refuted.argument: The benefit goes to the few users with huge tables, but the change applies to every session that uses replica role, and message #2 asks for a back-patch to all supported branches. The thread does not show any check of how existing tools run DDL under this setting. No documentation change is proposed, so those users get no notice.
refuted.author_must_show: Which existing tools run add foreign key or truncate under replica role today, and why is silently changing their result acceptable, especially in back branches?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of maintenance-fit-3, since its scenario depends on the back-patch.

touch_points.label: WAL / replication / standby
touch_points.reason: Logical replication apply workers run with session_replication_role = replica, so the truncate change may reach replicated truncate on subscribers.

touch_points.label: catalog changes
touch_points.reason: The proposal does not say whether pg_constraint marks the unchecked foreign key as validated.

touch_points.label: SQL-standard conflict or non-standard syntax
touch_points.reason: Plain add foreign key would skip the check of existing rows, beside the existing `not valid` spelling.

touch_points.label: new GUC
touch_points.reason: No new GUC, but session_replication_role grows from trigger firing to skipping DDL checks.

touch_points.label: planner behaviour change
touch_points.reason: The planner uses validated foreign keys for join estimates, and the constraint may be recorded as validated without a check.

touch_points.label: pg_dump / restore round-trip
touch_points.reason: A dump of a table with orphan rows under such a constraint fails at add foreign key on restore.

touch_points.label: security / privileges
touch_points.reason: A role with set on session_replication_role and truncate on the referenced table gains a new ability.

touch_points.label: backpatchability
touch_points.reason: Message #2 asks to back-patch to all supported branches, which removes two errors in minor releases.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
touch_points.reason: Tests of the setting inside tablecmds.c invite the same special case for other constraint types.

touch_points.label: doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)
touch_points.reason: `add foreign key ... not valid` already skips the scan of existing rows.

questions: Which replication or load workflow needs truncate of a referenced table under replica role, and how does it differ from the case closed in [P9]?
What does the replica setup need that `add foreign key ... not valid` cannot give, and is the new constraint marked convalidated in pg_constraint?
What rule decides which DDL checks session_replication_role = replica may skip, so that check, not null and unique validation do not follow by the same argument?
Does the truncate bypass apply inside the logical replication apply worker, where a replicated truncate could orphan subscriber-local referencing rows?
Which documented promise does the current behaviour break, so that removing two errors in minor releases is justified?

committability.owner_note: Someone who knows foreign key DDL in tablecmds.c and the logical replication apply path. The author asked Álvaro for review in message #9, and no committer has replied on the design.
committability.liability: The owner signs for foreign keys that may hold orphan rows while pg_dump, restore and the planner trust them, and for a wider meaning of session_replication_role, in every branch that gets the change.
committability.author_follow_up: The author has rebased the patch and moved the entry across CommitFests for over a year, and answered the reviewer in message #8.

priority.reason: The patch is about 6 KiB in tablecmds.c plus tests, and the stated need is foreign key creation on very large tables after an initial copy. The entry has been in 7 CommitFests without a design reply, because the relation to `not valid`, the catalog state and the scope of the setting are open.

provisional_note: Without the code, this review could not check whether the constraint is marked convalidated, whether the apply worker reaches the truncate bypass, or how truncate cascade and partitioned tables behave. Level 2 objections on those points were not evaluated.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: Reducing memory usage of creating foreign key between partitioned tables
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch makes RelationBuildPartitionDesc build a partitioned table's partition descriptor in a temporary memory context and delete that context afterwards, so the temporary memory is freed instead of being leaked. The aim was to stop the out-of-memory failures seen when adding a foreign key between two partitioned tables that each have thousands of partitions; later revisions were discussed for back-patching to v12.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane objected early that leak management belongs at the caller level, not inside RelationBuildPartitionDesc. Amit Langote then noted that commit 5b9312378 had already removed the repeated rebuild that caused the leak in v13, so the remaining question was back-patching. Tom Lane found no visible leak in HEAD and saw that the test case was still impractical because of planner cost in RI_Initial_Check, so he saw no reason to back-patch a leak fix. He recommended rejecting the patch and suggested back-porting 5b9312378 instead if a back-branch fix were wanted.

precedents_retrieved.title: Allow foreign keys to reference a superset of unique columns
precedents_retrieved.summary: Allow a foreign key constraint to reference a set of columns that is a superset of the columns of a non-deferrable unique or primary key index on the referenced table, rather than requiring an exact match. An optional USING INDEX clause after the referenced column list would name the supporting unique index where the choice would otherwise be ambiguous.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane objected that the semantics are questionable (for example CASCADE behaviour of the extra columns, nullable subset columns, MATCH PARTIAL and UNIQUE NULLS NOT DISTINCT), that the change could break existing optimizations, and that it risks conflict with the SQL standard and its information_schema. He said a patch was premature unless the SQL committee standardized the behaviour. Peter Eisentraut said that working out the full specification was the open work still required of the proposal.

precedents_retrieved.title: TRUNCATE behavior when session_replication_role = replica
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch makes TRUNCATE skip foreign key checks when session_replication_role = replica, the same way DELETE, INSERT and UPDATE already do. Peter Eisentraut proposed the opposite instead: create constraint triggers as TRIGGER_FIRES_ALWAYS so foreign keys are always enforced on replicas.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Peter Eisentraut argued that the current DELETE behaviour, which lets replicas hold data that violates foreign keys, is bad and should not be extended to TRUNCATE. He also saw no case for the change being needed. He closed the entry because the updated implementation of logical decoding of TRUNCATE no longer needed it.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
This part of the patch didn't end up being necessary, since the updated
implementation of logical decoding of TRUNCATE could do without it.

precedents_retrieved.title: TRUNCATE on foreign tables
precedents_retrieved.summary: Add an optional ExecForeignTruncate callback to FdwRoutine so that TRUNCATE works on foreign tables, including foreign partitions of a partitioned table. The callback gets the foreign tables of one server as a list, with DropBehavior and restart_seqs, and postgres_fdw sends one remote TRUNCATE for them.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Michael Paquier marked it returned with feedback because the implementation, the docs and the tests needed more work. The open issues at that point were ONLY handling, since TRUNCATE ONLY on a local foreign table could truncate the whole inheritance tree on the remote server, and a possible separate truncatable option for postgres_fdw. Missing postgres_fdw documentation and missing inheritance tests were also still open.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: For now, as the patch needs more work for its implementation, docs and tests, I am marking it as returned with feedback.

precedents_retrieved.title: TRUNCATE on foreign tables
precedents_retrieved.summary: Add an optional FDW callback, ExecForeignTruncate, that ExecuteTruncateGuts calls for foreign tables, so TRUNCATE works on them, including partitioned tables with foreign leaves. postgres_fdw would use it to send TRUNCATE to the remote server, grouping relations by server and passing ONLY and CASCADE/RESTRICT through.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The v5 patch from March 2020 stopped applying to HEAD because of conflicts in the postgres_fdw expected test output. Daniel Gustafsson asked for a rebase in July, and the visible messages show no reply from the author. The entry was then closed as stalled. Earlier, in January, Michael Paquier had returned the patch because its implementation, docs and tests needed more work.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: As this has stalled, I've marked this patch Returned with Feedback.

precedents_retrieved.title: Synchronize logical replication slots from primary to standby
precedents_retrieved.summary: A background worker on a physical standby periodically fetches logical replication slot information from the primary, so that after failover a logical subscriber finds up-to-date slots on the new primary. Later versions added synchronize_slot_names on the standby to pick which slots to sync, and standby_slot_names on the primary to hold logical replication back until the listed physical standbys catch up.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Andres Freund found that the patch breaks the catalog_xmin guarantee: row versions still needed for logical decoding on the standby can be removed. He said it needs a mechanism such as the "Minimal logical decoding on standbys" patch, which the author said was not near ready. Reviewers also objected to the blocking wait and the per-commit work added to reorderbuffer.c, and to the worker-per-database design tied to the logical replication launcher. The author listed these and an open configuration design as significant jobs still to do.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: The patch as-is just breaks one of the fundamental guarantees necessary for logical decoding, that no rows versions can be removed that are still required for logical decoding (signalled via catalog_xmin).

precedents_retrieved.title: An attempt to avoid locally-committed-but-not-replicated-to-standby-transactions in synchronous replication
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds a GUC, synchronous_replication_naptime_before_cancel, that makes a backend keep waiting for the sync standby ack for a set time before it handles a query cancel or proc die. A second part, not yet coded, would make the primary wait for sync standbys to catch up after a crash restart before it serves the locally committed transactions.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The entry was returned with feedback because the patch received no update for six months and no longer applied. The design was still open at the last author message. The author could not reliably detect, at restart, that a backend died while waiting for the sync replication ack, and the alternative of always waiting could keep the primary down. Earlier, Laurenz Albe objected that the approach still left some cases of transactions committed locally but not on the standby.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Since there hasn't been any updates for the past six months, and the patch
hasn't applied for a few months, I am marking this returned with feedback for
now.

precedents_retrieved.title: Respect client-initiated CopyDone during logical streaming replication
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch makes the walsender honor a client-initiated CopyDone during logical streaming, both while waiting for WAL and while ReorderBufferCommit sends a large transaction, so a client can return to command mode without closing the connection. Later versions added a continue_decoding_cb callback in the reorder buffer and taught pg_recvlogical to send CopyDone on SIGINT, with TAP tests.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Andres Freund objected to adding another callback and suggested raising an error in the prepare write callback, since a partial transaction may already have been sent when decoding stops. The author asked how this should work for output plugins that send only at commit, and the reviewers did not follow up. No updated patch appears, and the entry was marked returned with feedback; the visible messages do not show the final withdrawal.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: I don't think it's a good idea to return a non-error state if a command is interrupted in the middle. We might already have sent a partial transaction or such.
